newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Becton Dickinson to raise Asian profile.
newsitem.headline: Becton Dickinson to raise Asian profile.

text.p: U.S. medical products group Becton, Dickinson & Co said on Thursday it planned to boost investments in India and China by more than US$100 million over the next five years, and double Asian sales every three yeas.
Eugenio Naschold, the company's president for the Asia-Pacific region, said Becton also planned to expand its sales and marketing more aggressively in South Korea.
Becton's investments in Singapore will focus on making it the company's regional centre for research and development aimed at producing new and higher-value-added product lines, he said.

"Because of the aggressive investments, we expect to double our sales every three years or so," Naschold told Reuters in a telephone interview. "Definitely, we expect much better profitability and we now have a higher order of sales."

Given the growing concern over the spread of AIDS in Asia and the ability to spend more on health care as regional incomes rise, the company hopes to get the public to ask doctors for slightly more expensive -- but more sanitary -- disposable medical devices, he said.
"A large portion of the Indian population still reuses the old type of glass syringes," Naschold said. "But a majority can already afford the plastic disposable syringes."
"The cost of a disposable hypodermic syringe is equivalent, more or less, to a cigarette. If one can smoke 10,000 cigarettes a year, he can spend on three to four syringes a year."
Becton Dickinson already has invested $6 million in a facility at Bawal in Haryana state, north India, that will start production of intravenous and hypodermic syringes in September.
Two weeks ago, Becton's board approved an additional $40 million to expand capacity at the Bawal plant. Work on the expansion will start in April and be completed in 18 months.
"We forsee in the next five years we will be investing a total of $100 million in India, including the existing investments," Naschold said.
By taking advantage of low manufacturing costs in India, Becton plans to sell its products there and in other countries in the subcontinent and Middle East, he said.

Becton also plans to boost investments in China to between $80 million and $100 million over the next five years from the current $40 million. It has a plant in the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park in Jiangsu Province.

"We believe this will be the first step in production to reach only part of the Chinese population," he said. "As soon as we are confident that we can be efficient in the production of low cost syringes and gain experience in the China market...production at this plant will be almost doubled in the next five years."

Becton Dickinson operates in more than 80 countries. Among its products are drug delivery and infusion systems, diabetes care and vaccination devices, surgical devices, microbiology and blood collection products.
